verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 3 resolves the prior major finding. The fence stripper now follows the security-relevant Markdown boundaries: it accepts 0–3 spaces of indentation, retains the opening delimiter character and run length, and closes only on the same delimiter with a sufficient run and whitespace-only suffix. The added adversarial rows cover each previously identified divergence and include a valid-close/genuine-receipt control, so the tests are not vacuous. The writer-side choke point neutralizes the reserved namespace before App-authored publication, while the reader independently requires a whole, unquoted line; the sink-level tests verify both the direct conflict body and escalation body and confirm hostile content remains visible but inert. I found no remaining correctness, soundness, test-validity, or security issue in the diff.
